risk_of_bias.why: Overall critical is fair: pooled GDP-level regression with no controls or fixed effects and no reverse-causality strategy; confounding (critical, agree): no controls or strategy; exposure (serious, agree): telecom investment and staff are sector inputs, a partial proxy for ICT; selection (serious, agree): 7 of 25 economies dropped for missing data and the Leaders/Followers split was derived from earlier efficiency analyses of the same data; outcome (moderate, agree): GDP in current US$ levels, not per capita, not growth; specification (too_lenient, should be critical): the Leaders row repeats the complete-set coefficients (42.8020, 43.9723, 57.4954) with different p-values, the intercept is suppressed, and signs are not printed, so Table 1 cannot be trusted; selective reporting (too_harsh, moderate): all three pre-stated hypotheses H10, H20 and H30 are reported, though squared terms and the intercept are omitted and there are no robustness checks.

problems: Table 1 prints identical coefficients for the complete set and Leaders (42.8020, 43.9723, 57.4954) with different p-values, a probable table error. No minus signs appear anywhere in the extracted table; directions rest on the prose. Leaders have 66 and Followers 114 data points (sum 180), so groups are not a whole number of 10-year country series. Title says growth but the dependent variable is log GDP in current US$ levels. The record's notes already flag the sign and duplicate-row issues. Nothing else invented or mixed up.
